qt: to the Commission Gerald Hauser (PfE) Subject:

The return of the wolf as a result of its strict protection status generates additional costs and a significant amount of work for our farmers. Wolf-proof fences must be purchased, erected and regularly maintained. Added to this are the costs of livestock guard dogs and additional herding. The EU supports such actions through various funding programmes. However, fences do not provide reliable protection and are therefore not a sustainable solution. Even appropriately constructed fences cannot always stop wolves and are expensive to purchase and maintain. The responsibility for protection against wolf attacks must not be unilaterally shifted onto farmers, while the wolf is under strict protection. Anyone who demands ever more onerous protective measures from farmers must also make clear what costs these will entail and who will bear them. Farmers and taxpayers are entitled to full and transparent accounting. 1.

What amounts have been approved and actually paid out since 2014 from EU funds for wolf protection fences and other practical herd protection measures (based on the most recent data available)? Please provide a breakdown by year, Member State and funding programme, as well as the EU-wide total.
What is the breakdown of this expenditure with regard to the construction, retrofitting and ongoing maintenance of protective fences, the use of livestock guard dogs and additional herding efforts?
What amounts were spent on research, administration and publicity relating to wolves and herd protection?
